examples.en: I sort the trash by type.
Could you tell the twins apart from the start?
I'm going to separate the items by color.
It's hard to tell the two words apart.

examples.ko: 일하는 시간과 쉬는 시간을 구분해서 지내요.
examples.en: I keep work time and rest time separate.
Please tell me slowly how to distinguish them.

explain: '구분하다'는 기준을 두고 나눌 때 써요. '구별하다'는 차이를 알아본다는 느낌이 더 강해요. 'A와 B를 구분하다', '~으로 구분하다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: 구분하다 is used when you divide things by some standard. 구별하다 leans more toward noticing the difference. It appears as 'A와 B를 구분하다' (tell A from B) or '~으로 구분하다' (divide into ~).

examples.en: The letter will be delivered tomorrow.
I hope my feelings get across well.
The meeting contents were passed on to all employees.
It takes a day for the news to reach people.
The message was not conveyed accurately.
The gift will be delivered safely.

explain: '전달되다'는 물건뿐 아니라 말, 소식, 마음처럼 눈에 안 보이는 것에도 써요. 하는 사람을 말할 때는 '전달하다'를 써요. '~에게 전달되다'처럼 받는 사람 뒤에 '에게'가 와요.
explain_en: 전달되다 works for objects and also for invisible things like words, news and feelings. When you name the person doing it, use 전달하다. The receiver takes 에게, as in '~에게 전달되다'.

examples.en: The game was stopped because of the rain.
The construction suddenly stops.
What do I do if the internet service is cut off?
I don't know why the class was stopped.
The power went out and the work ended up halted.
Service will be suspended starting tomorrow.

explain: '중단되다'는 하던 일이 어떤 이유로 멈출 때 써요. 내가 일부러 멈추면 '중단하다', 저절로 멈추면 '중단되다'예요. 공사, 경기, 서비스, 운행 같은 말과 자주 같이 나와요.
explain_en: 중단되다 is used when something in progress stops because of some cause. If you stop it on purpose it is 중단하다, and if it stops by itself it is 중단되다. It often goes with words like construction, game, service and operation.

examples.en: Enough sleep restores your strength.

examples.ko: 따뜻한 죽이 아픈 아이의 기운을 회복시켰어요.
examples.en: The warm porridge restored the sick child's strength.

examples.ko: 충분히 쉬면 지친 몸을 회복시킬 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you rest enough, you can bring your tired body back to health.
It takes time to restore trust.
This is an exercise that helps with recovery.
The government is trying to revive the economy.

explain: '회복하다'는 스스로 좋아질 때, '회복시키다'는 누가 또는 무엇이 좋아지게 만들 때 써요. 건강, 체력, 신뢰, 경제처럼 원래 상태가 있는 것에 써요.
explain_en: 회복하다 is when something gets better by itself, while 회복시키다 is when a person or thing makes it get better. It goes with things that have an original state, such as health, strength, trust and the economy.

examples.en: The rumor is blown way out of proportion.
I think the news is exaggerated.
The story got more exaggerated as it was passed on.
What you see in the ad is overstated.
Did what I said sound exaggerated?
That story might be exaggerated.

explain: '과장되다'는 이야기나 표현이 실제보다 커졌다고 볼 때 써요. 말하는 사람이 일부러 그러면 '과장하다'예요. 소문, 광고, 표현, 연기 같은 말과 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: 과장되다 describes a story or expression that has become bigger than reality. If the speaker does it on purpose, use 과장하다. It fits well with rumors, ads, expressions and acting.

examples.en: My friend often exaggerates stories.
Please don't exaggerate so much.
He overstated his skills.

examples.ko: 과장해서 말하면 하루 종일 기다린 것 같아요.
examples.en: If I exaggerate, it feels like I waited all day.
I'm uncomfortable around people who exaggerate.
You don't need to inflate your experience at an interview.

explain: '과장하다'는 하는 사람이 있는 말이에요. 같은 일을 '과장되다'로 쓰면 말한 사람보다 이야기가 어떻게 됐는지에 초점이 가요. '과장해서 말하다'가 자주 쓰는 모양이에요.
explain_en: 과장하다 has a person doing the exaggerating. With 과장되다 the focus moves from the speaker to what happened to the story. '과장해서 말하다' (to speak with exaggeration) is a common pattern.

examples.en: Minsu leads the meeting.
Our team took the lead on this event.
It's good when children take the lead in their own study.

examples.ko: 새로운 사업을 주도할 사람을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: We're looking for someone to lead the new business.
The one who drives the conversation is always my older sister.
He is leading the reform.

explain: '주도하다'는 앞장서서 이끌고 일이 가는 방향을 잡을 때 써요. '이끌다'보다 딱딱해서 회의, 사업, 대화, 개혁 같은 말과 자주 나와요. '학습을 주도하다'처럼 스스로 하는 모습에도 써요.
explain_en: 주도하다 means to take the front and set the direction of something. It is more formal than 이끌다 and often goes with meetings, business, conversation and reform. It also fits self-directed things like '학습을 주도하다' (to lead one's own study).

en: be pushed forward; be carried out

examples.en: The new plan will be pushed forward from next month.

examples.ko: 공원 만드는 일이 빠르게 추진되고 있어요.
examples.en: The park project is moving ahead quickly.
That project was driven by the city.
The plan went ahead as scheduled.
The work couldn't move forward for lack of money.
It is scheduled to go ahead within this year.

explain: '추진되다'는 계획이나 사업이 실제로 진행될 때 써요. '계획이 추진되다', '사업이 추진되다'처럼 계획이나 정책이 주어예요. 뉴스와 공문에서 많이 보여요. 사람이 하면 '계획을 추진하다'예요.
explain_en: 추진되다 is used when a plan or project actually goes forward. Plans and policies are the subject, as in '계획이 추진되다'. It shows up a lot in news and official documents. When a person does it, use '계획을 추진하다'.

examples.en: The team leader pushes the plan forward.
The company moved the new business forward quickly.
We need more people to move the work forward.
Who will push this work ahead?
There's not enough drive to push the plan forward.

examples.ko: 예산을 정해야 일을 추진시킬 수 있어요.
examples.en: You have to set the budget before you can push the work forward.

explain: '추진시키다'는 '추진하다'와 뜻이 거의 같지만 쓰는 일이 드물어요. 대화와 글에서는 '계획을 추진하다'를 먼저 익히세요.
explain_en: 추진시키다 means almost the same as 추진하다 but is used much less. Learn '계획을 추진하다' first for talk and writing.

en: be based on; be founded on

examples.en: This movie is based on a true story.
You have to write something based on facts.
The plan was based on the survey results.
I'll speak based on my experience.
We decided on the basis of the law.

examples.ko: 자료에 기초하지 않은 주장은 믿기 어려워요.
examples.en: A claim not based on data is hard to believe.

explain: '기초하다'는 항상 '~에 기초하다'로 써요. 조사 '에'를 빠뜨리지 마세요. '기초한'처럼 꾸미는 모양으로 '사실에 기초한 이야기'라고 많이 말해요.
explain_en: 기초하다 is always used as '~에 기초하다' (be based on ~), so don't drop the particle 에. The modifier form is common, as in '사실에 기초한 이야기' (a story based on facts).

examples.en: The small shops join forces.
The two countries formed an alliance.
The students joined together and held an event.

examples.ko: 우리 동아리는 다른 동아리와 연합할 거예요.
examples.en: Our club will team up with another club.
Groups that join forces are growing in number.

examples.ko: 힘을 모으려고 연합했지만 결과는 좋지 않았어요.
examples.en: We joined forces to combine strength, but the result wasn't good.

explain: '연합하다'는 둘 이상의 단체나 나라가 하나의 목적으로 손을 잡을 때 써요. '같이 하다'보다 딱딱하고 '~와 연합하다'로 써요. 개인 두 사람이 힘을 합칠 때는 '힘을 합치다'를 더 자주 말해요.
explain_en: 연합하다 is used when two or more groups or countries join hands for one purpose. It is more formal than 같이 하다 and appears as '~와 연합하다'. For two individuals combining efforts, people more often say 힘을 합치다.

examples.en: A lot of money is invested in this business.
Time was invested in studying.

examples.ko: 그 돈은 새 공장에 투자될 거예요.
examples.en: The money will be invested in a new factory.
The amount invested grows every year.
I'm worried because the money isn't being invested properly.
The money invested in the research isn't wasted.

explain: '투자되다'는 돈이나 시간, 노력이 어디에 쓰였는지 말할 때 써요. '~에 투자되다'로 쓰고, 투자하는 사람을 말하면 '투자하다'를 써요.
explain_en: 투자되다 tells where money, time or effort has been put. It takes 에, as in '~에 투자되다'. When you name the person who invests, use 투자하다.

examples.en: The company forces overtime.
My parents don't force me to study.
No one can force you to attend.
Complaints came up after the rule was imposed.
I dislike an atmosphere where everyone is forced to attend.

examples.ko: 법으로 마스크 착용을 강제한 적이 있어요.
examples.en: At one time, wearing masks was made mandatory by law.

explain: '강제하다'는 싫어도 하게 만든다는 뜻이라 느낌이 강해요. 일상에서는 '억지로 시키다'나 '시키다'를 더 많이 써요. '강제'는 법이나 규칙처럼 힘이 있는 쪽이 할 때 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: 강제하다 means making someone do something even if they don't want to, so it sounds strong. In daily talk people use 억지로 시키다 or 시키다 more. 강제 fits when a side with power, like a law or a rule, does it.

examples.en: Korean words correspond to English words.

examples.ko: 표를 보면 숫자가 글자와 대응된다는 걸 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you look at the table, you can see the numbers match the letters.

examples.ko: 이 말은 영어로 정확히 대응되지 않아요.
examples.en: This word doesn't have an exact English counterpart.
Find the answer that matches each question.
The colors are matched to numbers.
Connect them with a line so they correspond to each other.

explain: '대응되다'는 두 개가 서로 짝이 맞을 때 써요. '~에 대응되다'로 말하고, 번역이나 표, 문제와 답 같은 설명에 자주 나와요. 상황에 맞게 행동하는 '대응하다'와는 달라요.
explain_en: 대응되다 is used when two things pair up with each other, as in '~에 대응되다'. It often appears in explanations about translation, tables, and questions and answers. It differs from 대응하다, which means to respond to a situation.

examples.en: Our company is entering overseas markets.
The Korean team advanced to the finals.
That singer will break into the US market.
I want to make my way into the film industry.
More women are entering the workforce.

examples.ko: 유명한 커피 가게가 우리 동네에 진출했대요.
examples.en: I heard a famous coffee chain has moved into our neighborhood.

explain: '진출하다'는 새로운 곳이나 분야, 다음 단계로 나아갈 때 써요. 스포츠에서는 '결승에 진출하다'처럼 다음 경기로 올라간다는 뜻으로 많이 말해요. '~에 진출하다'로 써요.
explain_en: 진출하다 is used for moving into a new place, field or next stage. In sports it is very common, as in '결승에 진출하다' (to reach the finals). It takes 에, as in '~에 진출하다'.

examples.en: The wizard in the story uses magic.
Children like magic stories.
The problem was solved like magic.
Shall we recite a magic spell?

examples.ko: 눈이 오자 마을은 마법에 걸린 것 같았어요.
examples.en: When snow fell, the town looked as if under a spell.

examples.ko: 저는 어렸을 때 마법사가 되고 싶었어요.
examples.en: When I was little I wanted to be a wizard.

explain: '마법'은 이야기 속의 힘을 말해요. 손으로 하는 '마술'은 사람이 보여 주는 기술이라 달라요. '마법사', '마법의 힘'처럼 말하고 비유로 놀랍게 잘 풀린 일에도 써요.
explain_en: 마법 is the power found in stories. 마술 is a performed trick done by a person, so they differ. You say 마법사 (wizard) or 마법의 힘 (magic power), and the word is also used figuratively for something that worked out amazingly well.

examples.en: I prove that I am a student.
This document proves my age.
He proved his skill at the competition.
I'll prove it with results rather than words.
Is there a way to prove it?

examples.ko: 신분을 증명할 수 있는 카드가 필요해요.
examples.en: You need a card that can prove your identity.

explain: '증명하다'는 서류나 결과로 사실을 보여 줄 때 써요. 신분이나 나이는 '신분증으로 증명하다'처럼 말해요. 비슷한 '확인하다'는 맞는지 살펴보는 쪽이에요.
explain_en: 증명하다 is used when you show that something is true through documents or results. For identity or age you say '신분증으로 증명하다' (prove with an ID). The similar 확인하다 leans toward checking whether something is correct.

examples.en: This app is used in class.
The leftover ingredients were used in another dish.
AI is being used in many places.

examples.ko: 잘 활용되지 않는 방이 하나 있어요.
examples.en: There's a room that isn't put to good use.
The range of uses keeps widening.

examples.ko: 이 자료는 시험 공부에 활용될 거예요.
examples.en: These materials will be used for exam study.

explain: '활용되다'는 가진 것이 쓸모 있게 쓰일 때 써요. 그냥 '쓰이다'보다 잘 살려 쓴다는 느낌이 들어요. '~에 활용되다'로 써요.
explain_en: 활용되다 is used when something one has is put to useful work. Compared with plain 쓰이다, it gives the feel of being used well. It appears as '~에 활용되다'.

examples.en: My father does labor in a factory.
I worked eight hours a day.
People who labor need days off.
After physical work, the meal tastes great.

examples.ko: 어릴 때부터 노동할 수밖에 없었던 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people had no choice but to work from a young age.
I'm tired from working since early morning.

explain: '노동하다'는 몸이나 힘을 써서 일하고 돈을 번다는 느낌이 있어요. 평소 대화에서는 '일하다'를 더 많이 써요. '노동자', '노동 시간' 같은 말이 자주 나와요.
explain_en: 노동하다 carries the feel of working with body or strength to earn a living. In everyday talk 일하다 is used far more often. It is useful to learn it together with words like 노동자 (worker) and 노동 시간 (working hours).

examples.en: An expensive gift feels like a burden.
Tomorrow's presentation weighed on me too much.

examples.ko: 집값이 너무 부담되면 이사하는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: If the housing cost is too much of a burden, moving is a good idea.
Please tell me ahead of time about anything that feels like a burden.
It's a lot of money for me, so I think it'll be a burden.
Let's eat something simple so the bill isn't a burden.

explain: '부담되다'는 돈이나 일, 마음이 무겁게 느껴질 때 써요. '부담스럽다'를 더 자주 말해요. 상대에게 '부담 갖지 마세요'라고 하면 신경 쓰지 말라는 따뜻한 인사예요.
explain_en: 부담되다 is used when money, work or feelings seem heavy. In Korean 부담스럽다 is said more often. '부담 갖지 마세요' to someone is a kind way of saying don't worry about it.

examples.en: I don't want to burden my friend with the work.
You must not make the customers bear the cost.
The company made employees pay for training.
They put too much on the child.
I'm sorry, it feels like I'm putting a load on you.
We can't place the caregiving burden on the family.

explain: '부담시키다'는 남에게 짐이나 비용을 지게 한다는 뜻이라 조금 딱딱해요. 대화에서는 '부담을 주다'를 더 자주 써요. 비용은 '~에게 비용을 부담시키다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: 부담시키다 means making another person carry a load or cost, and it sounds a bit stiff. In conversation 부담을 주다 is more common. For costs you say '~에게 비용을 부담시키다'.

examples.en: The company covers the transportation cost.
I'll cover the meal bill.
Who paid for the repairs?
If we split it in half, the load gets lighter.
The person who will bear the cost has been decided.
Everyone has to share the tax burden together.

explain: '부담하다'는 비용이나 책임을 자기가 맡을 때 써요. 돈을 낼 때는 '내다'보다 공식적이에요. '비용을 부담하다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: 부담하다 is used when you take on a cost or responsibility yourself. It is more formal than 내다 (to pay). It appears in phrases like '비용을 부담하다' (to bear the cost).

en: win the championship; take first place

examples.en: Our team wins the championship.
A Korean player won the tournament.
I will win the title this year for sure.
Everyone shouted the moment they won.
You have to practice hard to win the title.
He is a player who won three times in a row.

explain: '우승하다'는 대회에서 일등을 할 때 써요. 대회 이름은 '~에서 우승하다'로 말해요. 일상의 '일등 하다'나 '이기다'는 시합 하나를 이길 때도 쓰지만 '우승'은 전체 결과예요.
explain_en: 우승하다 is used when you take first place in a tournament. The event takes 에서, as in '~에서 우승하다'. 이기다 can mean winning a single match, but 우승 refers to the overall result.

examples.en: I log on to the site every morning.
I connected to the server, but it's slow.
You need a password to connect to the Wi-Fi.
Too many people are connecting right now.

examples.ko: 집에서 접속할 수 있는 방법이 있어요?
examples.en: Is there a way to connect from home?
An error window popped up as soon as I connected.

explain: '접속하다'는 인터넷이나 서버에 연결해서 들어갈 때 써요. 사이트에 들어가는 일은 '접속하다', 로그인은 계정으로 들어가는 일이라 달라요. 'IP에 접속하다'처럼 연결하는 대상 뒤에 '에'가 와요.
explain_en: 접속하다 is used when you connect to and enter the internet or a server. Going into a site is 접속하다, while logging in means entering with an account, so the two differ. The target takes 에, as in 'IP에 접속하다'.

examples.en: This company builds apartment buildings.
My grandfather built the house himself.
They will build a library next to the school.
It took three years to build.
You have to get a permit before building.
I want to build a hanok.

explain: '건축하다'는 집이나 건물처럼 큰 구조물을 지을 때 써요. '짓다'는 집, 밥, 옷, 이름까지 두루 쓰지만 '건축하다'는 건물에만 써요. '건축가'와 같은 말도 같이 알아 두세요.
explain_en: 건축하다 is used for building large structures like houses and buildings. 짓다 is used widely, for houses, meals, clothes and even names, while 건축하다 is only for buildings. Learn 건축가 (architect) along with it.

examples.en: Our school has exchanges with a Japanese school.
I often interacted with friends from abroad.
The two countries decided to exchange cultures.
Interacting with other people broadens your view.
There's a group that interacts online.

examples.ko: 앞으로도 서로 교류할 수 있으면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I hope we can keep in touch with each other.

explain: '교류하다'는 사람이나 단체, 나라가 서로 오가며 문화나 생각을 나눌 때 써요. '교류'는 꾸준한 관계라는 느낌이 있어서 한 번만 만나는 일에는 잘 안 써요. '~와/과 교류하다'로 말해요.
explain_en: 교류하다 is used when people, groups or countries go back and forth sharing culture or ideas. 교류 gives the feel of an ongoing relationship, so it is not used much for a single meeting. It appears as '~와/과 교류하다'.

examples.en: Don't butt into other people's business.

examples.ko: 저는 그 일에 상관하고 싶지 않아요.
examples.en: I don't want to get involved in that matter.
I don't care who comes.
Why does my younger sibling interfere in my business?

examples.ko: 제가 뭘 하든 상관하지 말아 주세요.
examples.en: Please don't interfere in whatever I do.

examples.ko: 친구가 그 일에 상관했다가 오히려 오해를 받았어요.
examples.en: My friend got involved in that matter and ended up being misunderstood.

explain: '상관하다'는 '~에 상관하다'처럼 일에 끼어들거나 신경 쓸 때 써요. 실제 대화에서는 '상관없다'(괜찮다, 관계없다)와 '상관하지 마세요'(참견하지 마세요)를 가장 많이 말해요. 뒤의 말은 조금 차갑게 들릴 수 있어요.
explain_en: 상관하다 means to get involved in or care about something, as in '~에 상관하다'. In real conversation the most common forms are 상관없다 (it doesn't matter) and 상관하지 마세요 (don't butt in). The latter can sound a bit cold.

examples.en: Everyone, please pay attention to this picture.
People are paying attention to the new singer.
The teacher took note of that point.
There's some news worth noting.
A tournament the world is watching is being held.

examples.ko: 먼저 이 숫자에 주목하고 읽어 보세요.
examples.en: First look closely at this number and then read.

explain: '주목하다'는 눈과 마음을 한곳에 모을 때 써요. 발표나 수업에서 '주목해 주세요'라고 하면 모두 앞을 보라고 부탁하는 거예요. '~에 주목하다'로 써요.
explain_en: 주목하다 means focusing your eyes and mind on one point. In a talk or class, '주목해 주세요' means everyone please look at me. It appears as '~에 주목하다'.

examples.en: This job requires a special skill.
The situation is a bit unusual.
It is allowed only in special cases.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 특수하게 만든 옷을 팔아요.
examples.en: That company sells specially made clothes.
The environment was unusual, so it was hard to adapt.

examples.ko: 이곳은 특수했던 시대의 이야기를 담고 있어요.
examples.en: This place holds a story from a special era.

explain: '특수하다'는 보통과 달라서 한정된 경우나 목적에 맞다는 느낌이에요. '특별하다'는 좋은 의미로 소중하거나 뛰어나다고 말할 때 더 많이 써요. '특수 효과', '특수 상황'처럼 붙여서도 써요.
explain_en: 특수하다 carries the feel of being different from the usual and fitted to a limited case or purpose. 특별하다 is used more when saying something is precious or outstanding in a good way. It also attaches to nouns, as in 특수 효과 (special effects) and 특수 상황 (special situation).

examples.en: A giant tree watches over the village.
Whales are truly enormous.
The waves were huge, so I was scared.
I was amazed at the hugely built building.
That company grew into a giant enterprise.
It was much bigger than it looked in photos.

explain: '거대하다'는 '크다'보다 훨씬 커서 놀랄 정도일 때 써요. 건물, 동물, 산, 기업처럼 눈에 띄게 큰 것에 잘 어울려요. 작은 물건이나 사람의 키에는 잘 안 써요.
explain_en: 거대하다 is used when something is far bigger than 크다, large enough to be startling. It fits buildings, animals, mountains and companies. It is not used much for small objects or a person's height.

examples.en: Participants are recruited this week.
A hundred volunteers were recruited.
I'll contact you as soon as staff are recruited.

examples.ko: 학생이 충분히 모집되지 않아서 수업이 취소됐어요.
examples.en: The class was canceled because not enough students signed up.
The people who were recruited will gather next week.
New members will soon be recruited.

explain: '모집되다'는 사람을 구하는 일이 진행되어 사람들이 모였을 때 써요. 구하는 쪽은 '모집하다'를 써요. 공고에서는 '모집 중'이나 '모집 마감'처럼 짧게 자주 써요.
explain_en: 모집되다 is used when a drive to find people has progressed and people have been gathered. The side doing the recruiting uses 모집하다. In notices you often see the short forms 모집 중 (now recruiting) and 모집 마감 (recruitment closed).

examples.ko: 그 사람은 건물을 세 채 소유해요.
examples.en: That person owns three buildings.
I don't own a car.
Who owned this land?
If you try to own everything, it's tiring.

examples.ko: 집을 소유한 사람만 신청할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Only people who own a house can apply.
My dream is to own a small shop.

explain: '소유하다'는 집, 땅, 회사처럼 법적으로 내 것인 큰 것을 말할 때 써요. 일상에서 '가지고 있다'나 '있다'를 더 자주 말해요. '소유'는 '소유권', '소유자'처럼 서류에서도 많이 나와요.
explain_en: 소유하다 is used for big things that are legally yours, like a house, land or a company. In daily life 가지고 있다 or 있다 is said more often. 소유 also appears a lot in documents, as in 소유권 (ownership) and 소유자 (owner).

examples.en: A piano piece is played in the concert hall.
That song was played on the guitar.

examples.ko: 이 곡은 결혼식에서 자주 연주되곤 해요.
examples.en: This piece is often played at weddings.
The music being played is really gentle.

examples.ko: 오늘 밤 새 곡이 처음 연주될 거예요.
examples.en: A new piece will be performed for the first time tonight.
The piece couldn't be played because there was no instrument.

explain: '연주되다'는 악기로 음악이 들릴 때 써요. 노래를 부르는 일에는 안 써요. '곡이 연주되다'처럼 곡이 주어예요. 사람이 하면 '피아노를 연주하다'예요.
explain_en: 연주되다 is used when music is heard from instruments. It isn't used for singing. The piece is the subject, as in '곡이 연주되다'. When a person does it, use '피아노를 연주하다'.

en: be secured; be retained; be reserved

examples.en: A meeting room for tomorrow has been secured.
A sufficient budget is secured.
I'll let you know once seats are secured.
Let's start first with the data we've secured.
The event was postponed because safety wasn't ensured.
Please wait until time has been set aside.

explain: '확보되다'는 필요한 것이 미리 마련되어 손에 들어올 때 써요. 자리, 시간, 예산, 자료, 안전처럼 정해진 목적에 쓸 것을 말해요. 하는 쪽을 말하면 '확보하다'예요.
explain_en: 확보되다 is used when something needed has been arranged ahead and is in hand. It fits things like seats, time, budget, data and safety that are for a set purpose. If you name who does it, use 확보하다.

examples.en: I stay close to good friends.
If you keep books close, your thinking gets deeper.
The closer children stay to nature, the healthier they get.
Don't go near the fire.

examples.ko: 저는 그 사람을 가까이하고 싶지 않아요.
examples.en: I don't want to be close to that person.
I've gotten into the habit of keeping exercise a regular part of my life.

explain: '가까이하다'는 사람, 책, 운동처럼 가까이 두고 자주 만난다는 뜻이에요. '책을 가까이하세요'는 책 읽는 습관을 들이라는 권유의 말이에요. 반대로 멀리하는 것은 '멀리하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: 가까이하다 means keeping something close and meeting it often, whether a person, books or exercise. '책을 가까이하세요' is advice to build a reading habit. The opposite, keeping away from something, is 멀리하다.

examples.en: I prepare for the chance of rain.
I study every day to prepare for the exam.
There was a drill to prepare for earthquakes.
I bought clothes in preparation for winter.
To prepare for later, you have to save.
I'll be ready for the worst case.

explain: '대비하다'는 일어날지 모르는 일을 미리 준비할 때 써요. '준비하다'는 해야 할 일을 갖추는 것이고, '대비하다'는 나쁜 일이나 변화에 맞서 갖추는 것이에요. 보통 '~에 대비하다'로 써요.
explain_en: 대비하다 is used when you prepare in advance for something that might happen. 준비하다 is getting ready for something you have to do, while 대비하다 is getting ready against bad events or change. It is usually '~에 대비하다'.

examples.en: Let's wrap up today's work here.
I closed the presentation with a greeting.
I'll finish the report by tomorrow.
I want to end it on a good note.
What's a good way to wrap up this year?
I rushed to finish and made a mistake.

explain: '마무리하다'는 일의 끝 부분을 잘 정리해 끝낼 때 써요. 그냥 '끝내다'보다 마지막 손질을 한다는 느낌이 있어요. '일을 마무리하다', '마무리 짓다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: 마무리하다 means tidying up and ending the last part of a task well. Compared with plain 끝내다, it gives the feel of putting on finishing touches. You say '일을 마무리하다' or '마무리 짓다'.

examples.en: That behavior is a little silly.
I felt like a fool.
It's a silly question, so I'm embarrassed.
The goofy look when you laugh is cute.
He may look foolish, but he has a warm heart.
I think my mistake last time was foolish.

explain: '바보스럽다'는 말이나 행동이 어리석어 보일 때 써요. 친한 사이에서는 귀엽고 어설프다는 뜻으로도 쓰지만 남에게 쓰면 기분 나쁠 수 있으니 조심하세요. '바보 같다'와 비슷하고, 내 모습에 쓰면 부드러워요.
explain_en: 바보스럽다 is used when words or actions look foolish. Among close people it can mean cute and clumsy, but said to others it can offend, so be careful. It is close to 바보 같다, and it sounds gentler when used about yourself.

en: be put on the market; be released

examples.en: The new album comes out tomorrow.
That game was released last year.
The new product is due to be released soon.
It sold out as soon as it was released.

examples.ko: 발매된 지 십 년이 넘은 음반이에요.
examples.en: It's a record that has been out for over ten years.
It hasn't been released in Korea yet.

explain: '발매되다'는 음반, 게임, 책, 물건이 처음 팔기 시작할 때 써요. 음악에서는 '출시'보다 '발매'를 더 많이 써요. 영화는 '개봉되다'를 써요.
explain_en: 발매되다 is used when a record, game, book or product goes on sale for the first time. For music, 발매 is used more often than 출시. For movies, use 개봉되다.

examples.en: Trash is separated by type.
The lid comes off easily.
The two rooms were divided by a wall.
When work and home are separate, my mind is at ease.
Please put the detached part back on.
It's a machine that can't be detached from the body.

explain: '분리되다'는 붙어 있던 것이 떨어질 때 써요. 내가 떼어 놓으면 '분리하다'예요. 쓰레기는 '분리수거'라고 해서 종류별로 나눠 버리는 일을 말해요.
explain_en: 분리되다 is used when something that was attached comes apart. If you detach it yourself it is 분리하다. For trash, 분리수거 means sorting waste by type for disposal.

examples.en: The child's expression looks uneasy.
I waited for the result with an uneasy heart.
He looked at the door uneasily.
The child walking alone looked uneasy.
His voice sounded uneasy, so I was worried.
If you look uneasy, I'll help you.

explain: '불안스럽다'는 겉으로 불안해 보이는 모습을 말할 때 써요. 내 기분을 말할 때는 '불안하다'를 더 자주 써요. '불안스러워 보이다'처럼 다른 사람을 보고 말하는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: 불안스럽다 describes a look or manner that appears anxious from outside. For your own feeling, 불안하다 is used more often. It is commonly used when watching someone else, as in '불안스러워 보이다' (look uneasy).

examples.en: I massage my grandmother's shoulders.
I gave my tired dad a massage.
Massaging your legs relieves tiredness.
We are massaging each other's shoulders.
I'll give my parents a massage this weekend.
I bought a machine that massages the hands.

explain: '안마하다'는 몸을 손으로 주물러 풀어 줄 때 써요. 부모님께 하면 '안마해 드리다'라고 높여요. 가게에서 받는 것은 '마사지'라는 말도 많이 써요.
explain_en: 안마하다 means kneading the body with the hands to relax it. For your parents you raise it to '안마해 드리다'. For the service you receive at a shop, the word 마사지 is also widely used.

examples.en: I doubt whether that's really true.
The result was strange, so it raised suspicion.
If you suspect a cold, go to the hospital.
If there's anything doubtful, please tell me.
This file is suspected to have a virus.
When in doubt, check again.

explain: '의심되다'는 '~이/가 의심되다'처럼 나쁜 일이나 거짓일 수 있다는 생각이 저절로 들 때 써요. 내가 일부러 의심하면 '의심하다'예요. 병원에서는 '감기가 의심되다'처럼 아직 확실하지 않은 병에 말해요.
explain_en: 의심되다 is used as '~이/가 의심되다' when a thought that something may be bad or false comes to mind by itself. If you doubt on purpose, it is 의심하다. At a clinic it is used for a not-yet-certain illness, as in '감기가 의심되다'.
